newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian bonds quietly confident ahead of budget.
newsitem.headline: Australian bonds quietly confident ahead of budget.

text.p: *Australian bond yields were slightly lower in fairly subdued trading ahead of the Federal budget, due to be handed down by Treasurer Peter Costello at 7.30 p.m. (0930 GMT).
Australian bond yields were slightly lower in fairly subdued trading ahead of the Federal budget, due to be handed down by Treasurer Peter Costello at 7.30 p.m. (0930 GMT).

The June 10-year bond futures contract struck its highest level since late February at 92.365 at one stage, taking the benchmark 10-year bond yield down to around 7.60 percent, as the market anticipated a bond-friendly statement.
"I think the current rally has got about 10 basis points left in it on confirmation of the budget expectations, but from then on its down to the U.S.," one trader said.

Market analysts are expecting Costello to announce a substantial headline budget surplus, taking into account recent airport sales and the forthcoming partial sale of Telstra, which could see little or no net bond issuance in the fiscal year.

They are also expecting a further improvement in the underlying budget deficit with median expectations centring on a A$2.1 billion deficit for 1997/98 from a A$3.8 billion deficit starting point, according to a recent Reuters survey.
The run-up to this year's budget has been a fairly laid-back affair, and reaction to it could be relatively subdued unless there are any surprises, traders said.
The Sydney Futures Exchange (SFE) trading floor will be open for a special budget session between 7.00 p.m. and 8.15 p.m. (0900-1015 GMT).

The focus will immediately switch to the United States after the initial budget reaction withApril U.S. retail sales are due to be released later on Tuesday, along with key inflation reports later in the week.
Weak results are expected for the data and may give the U.S. Treasury market some guidence over the potential outcome to the May 20 Federal Open Market Committee meeting.

Long dated bonds outperformed the U.S. and Canada ahead of the budget. New Zealand debt found a bid tone again in response to a rising N.Z. TWI, having been sold-off on Monday on surprise remarks by the RBNZ that it would prefer somewhat firmer monetary conditions.
